message.content:
Below is a **7‑day “Paris in a Week” itinerary** that balances the classic sights with some off‑the‑beaten‑path experiences.  
Feel free to tweak the days or swap activities to match your interests (art, food, history, shopping, etc.). I’ve also added practical travel tips, budget estimates, and a few “hidden gems” that most tourists miss.

---

## 1️⃣ Pre‑Trip Checklist

| Item | Details |
|------|---------|
| **Passport & Visa** | Passport valid at least 6 months beyond your stay. EU/US/Canada/UK citizens can enter visa‑free for up to 90 days. Others may need a Schengen visa. |
| **Travel Insurance** | Covers health, trip cancellation, and lost luggage. |
| **Currency** | Euro (€). Credit cards work everywhere; carry a small amount of cash for markets and cafés. |
| **Packing** | Comfortable walking shoes, light layers (Paris weather can be unpredictable), universal power adapter, reusable water bottle. |
| **Apps** | Citymapper (public transport), Google Maps, TripAdvisor, Yelp, RATP (metro schedules), and a French phrasebook or translation app. |

---

## 2️⃣ Flights & Arrival

| Day | Flight Suggestion | Notes |
|-----|-------------------|-------|
| **Day 0** | Depart from your home city → Paris Charles de Gaulle (CDG) or Orly (ORY). | CDG is larger, ORY is closer to the city center. |
| **Arrival** | Take the RER B train from CDG to Gare du Nord (≈35 min, €10). ORY → RER B to Gare du Nord (≈30 min, €8). | From Gare du Nord, you’re within walking distance of many central neighborhoods. |

---

## 3️⃣ Accommodation

| Neighborhood | Why It’s Great | Sample Hotels (mid‑range) | Budget (per night) |
|--------------|----------------|---------------------------|--------------------|
| **Le Marais** | Trendy boutiques, historic streets, great cafés. | Hôtel Henriette, Hotel Caron | €120–€180 |
| **Latin Quarter** | Bohemian vibe, close to Notre‑Dame, student-friendly. | Hotel des Arts, Hotel L'Arc | €100–€160 |
| **Saint‑Germain‑en‑Laye** | Quiet, upscale, near Luxembourg Gardens. | Hotel Le Six, Hotel Le Meurice | €200–€300 |
| **Montmartre** | Artistic heritage, panoramic views. | Hotel Montmartre, Hotel Le Relais | €110–€170 |

*Tip:* Book a hotel with a kitchenette if you plan to cook a few meals; it saves money and lets you enjoy local markets.

---

## 4️⃣ 7‑Day Itinerary

> **Note:** All times are approximate; adjust based on opening hours and personal pace.

### **Day 1 – Classic Landmarks**

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 09:00 | **Eiffel Tower** – Arrive early to avoid crowds. Take the elevator to the 2nd floor (skip the 3rd for a cheaper ticket). |
| 11:30 | Walk along the Seine to **Trocadéro Gardens** for iconic tower photos. |
| 12:30 | Lunch at **Café Constant** (Marais) – try quiche Lorraine. |
| 14:00 | **Champs‑Élysées** – stroll, window shop, visit **Arc de Triomphe** (climb to the top). |
| 16:30 | **Louvre Museum** – pre‑book tickets; focus on the Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, and the Egyptian wing. |
| 19:30 | Dinner at **Le Comptoir du Relais** (Latin Quarter) – classic French bistro. |

### **Day 2 – Art & Culture**

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 09:00 | **Musée d’Orsay** – Impressionist masterpieces. |
| 12:00 | Picnic at **Jardin des Tuileries** – grab baguettes, cheese, and wine from a nearby market. |
| 13:30 | **Centre Pompidou** – modern art, quirky architecture. |
| 15:30 | Explore **Le Marais** – vintage shops, Picasso Museum. |
| 18:00 | **Dinner** at **L’As du Fallafel** (for a casual bite) or **Chez Janou** (for a more refined experience). |
| 20:30 | Optional: Attend a jazz club in **Le Caveau de la Huchette**. |

### **Day 3 – Day Trip to Versailles**

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 08:30 | Take the RER C from **Saint‑Germain‑en‑Laye** to **Versailles Château** (≈45 min). |
| 09:30 | Guided tour of the palace (skip the Hall of Mirrors if you’re short on time). |
| 12:00 | Lunch at **La Petite Venise** (inside the gardens). |
| 13:30 | Explore the **Grand Trianon** and **Queen’s Hamlet**. |
| 15:30 | Return to Paris via RER C. |
| 18:00 | Dinner at **Le Petit Cler** (market street). |

### **Day 4 – Hidden Gems & Shopping**

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 09:00 | **Marché aux Puces de Saint‑Ouen** – flea market for vintage finds. |
| 12:00 | Lunch at **Café des Deux Moulins** (from *Amélie*). |
| 13:30 | **Sainte‑Clotilde** – a lesser‑known basilica with beautiful mosaics. |
| 15:00 | **Galeries Lafayette** – rooftop terrace for skyline views. |
| 17:00 | **Rue Montorgueil** – food stalls, bakeries, and a lively atmosphere. |
| 19:30 | Dinner at **Le Relais de l’Entrecôte** (famous steak‑and‑french fries). |

### **Day 5 – Montmartre & Sacré‑Coeur**

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 09:00 | **Sacré‑Coeur Basilica** – climb to the dome for panoramic city views. |
| 10:30 | Wander the cobblestone streets, visit **Place du Tertre** (artists’ square). |
| 12:00 | Lunch at **Le Consulat** (historic café). |
| 13:30 | **Espace Dalí** – surrealist art. |
| 15:00 | **Moulin Rouge** – take a photo outside; consider a backstage tour. |
| 18:00 | Dinner at **La Maison Rose** (iconic pink café). |
| 20:30 | Optional: Attend a cabaret show at **Moulin Rouge** or **Lido**. |

### **Day 6 – Parks & Relaxation**

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 09:00 | **Luxembourg Gardens** – stroll, visit the Medici Fountain. |
| 11:00 | **Pantheon** – see the tombs of Voltaire, Rousseau, and Marie Curie. |
| 12:30 | Lunch at **Café de Flore** (left‑wing) – classic Parisian café. |
| 14:00 | **Notre‑Dame Cathedral** – admire the façade (the interior may still be under restoration). |
| 15:30 | **Île de la Cité** – walk across the Pont Neuf. |
| 17:00 | **Sainte‑Sulpice** – beautiful Baroque interior. |
| 19:00 | Dinner at **Le Coupe Chou** (cozy, romantic). |
| 21:00 | Evening stroll along the Seine, perhaps a river cruise (Bateaux Mouches). |

### **Day 7 – Departure / Last‑Minute Shopping**

| Time | Activity |
|------|----------|
| 08:00 | Breakfast at **Du Pain et des Idées** (famous croissants). |
| 09:30 | Quick visit to **Musée Rodin** (if you missed it earlier). |
| 11:00 | Last‑minute shopping at **Printemps** or **Le Bon Marché**. |
| 13:00 | Lunch at **L’Arpège** (if you’re feeling indulgent). |
| 15:00 | Head back to your hotel, collect luggage, and head to the airport. |

---

## 5️⃣ Budget Overview (per person)

| Category | Approx. Cost |
|----------|--------------|
| Flights (round‑trip) | €200–€600 (depending on origin & season) |
| Accommodation (7 nights) | €800–€2100 |
| Meals | €25–€50 per day (€175–€350 total) |
| Transport (metro + occasional taxi) | €30–€50 |
| Attractions (tickets, tours) | €150–€250 |
| Miscellaneous (souvenirs, tips) | €50–€100 |
| **Total** | **€1400–€3500** |

*(Prices are mid‑range; you can save by staying in hostels or using meal delivery services.)*

---

## 6️⃣ Hidden Gems & “Off‑the‑Beaten‑Path” Ideas

| Spot | Why It’s Worth It |
|------|-------------------|
| **Parc des Buttes‑Chaumont** | A hidden park with waterfalls, a temple, and a great view of the city. |
| **Musée de la Chasse et de la Nature** | Unique museum dedicated to hunting and nature art. |
| **La Promenade Plantée (Coulée Verte)** | Elevated green walkway built on an old railway viaduct. |
| **Rue Cremieux** | Colorful houses, perfect for Instagram. |
| **La Petite Ceinture** | Abandoned railway turned urban trail (great for a bike ride). |
| **Le Marché des Enfants Rouges** | Oldest covered market in Paris, great for lunch. |

---

## 7️⃣ Quick Tips

| Tip | Explanation |
|-----|-------------|
| **Buy tickets online** | Saves time at major attractions (Louvre, Eiffel Tower, Versailles). |
| **Use Citymapper** | Real‑time public transport info, best routes. |
| **Walk whenever possible** | Paris is very walkable; you’ll discover hidden cafés and shops. |
| **Try “bouchons”** | Traditional Lyonnais restaurants in the city for hearty meals. |
| **Stay hydrated** | Carry a reusable bottle; tap water is safe. |
| **Learn basic French phrases** | “Bonjour”, “Merci”, “Au revoir”, “Combien ça coûte?” go a long way. |

---

## 8️⃣ Final Thoughts

Paris is a city that rewards curiosity. Even with a packed itinerary, leave a little room for spontaneous detours—perhaps a street performer in Montmartre or a pop‑up art exhibit in Le Marais. Enjoy the blend of history, culture, and culinary delights that make Paris unforgettable.

Bon voyage! 🚀✈️🇫🇷
